x: Eventually our lads finished in a procession with five consecutive placings from 18 to 22 and backed up by George Bentley, Joe Wilson and Joe Coleman, we succeeded in taking the Nijmegan Shield with our eight walkers in the first 48, an excellent performance on which all are to be congratulated.

Chief Judge was our own GEORGE BENTLEY and amongst those judging were FRED DENNY - happily recovered from his operation, FRANK JARVIS who has also had a bout in hospital, evergreen HAROLD KING with SYD SPENCER, HARRY SHIELDS and BILL TRUE to cast their eagle eyes on the proceedings.

The Chief Judge at the Chippenham to Calne Walk was George Bentley now living at Portishead, Avon. He looked fit and well and told us that his brother Fred, one of our great long-distance walkers of the 30's and an international in 1938, was also fit and well.

It was good to see the fit looking George Bentley amongst the Judges, the West Country obviously agrees with him. I was delighted when Judy Farr of Trowbridge introduced me to her Club mate Sheila Jennings, formerly of London Olumpiades.

Amongst the judges were George Bentley, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Sid Spencer, Bill True and Joe Wilson and refereeing was Ray Hall. Again the course was changed using three laps of the hills using a less steep hill than previous.
He served in the Army during the war and after the war resumed competing and was in the scoring team with George Bentley in The Garnet Cup race in 1948.

Eventually our lads finished in a procession with five consecutive placings from 18 to 22 and backed up by George Bentley, Joe Wilson and Joe Coleman, we succeeded in taking the Nijmegan Shield with our eight walkers in the first 48, an excellent performance on which all are to be congratulated.
